chunks: Amr ibn Sa'id narrated from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man whose head has sores and cannot perform al-halq (shaving the whole head), he said: 'If he has already performed hajj before this, let him perform al-jadhdh (partial shaving); and if he has not performed hajj, he must perform al-halq.'

And regarding a man who shaved before slaughting, he said: 'He should slaughter and repeat the shaving, because Allah, the Exalted, says: "And do not shave your heads until the offering reaches its place."'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who cannot shave their head due to sores or illness?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific conditions under which a pilgrim may substitute partial shaving (qasr) for complete shaving (halq) when physical impediments like sores prevent the latter. It emphasizes the strict chronological sequence of Hajj rituals, particularly the prohibition of shaving before the sacrificial animal reaches its designated place, a rule derived directly from the Quranic verse in Surah Al-Baqarah. This highlights the Shia scholarly focus on the precise order of acts (tartib) and the flexibility (rukhas) granted for genuine physical hardship.
